analysis.headline: 60,000 Migrants Enter Spain's Ceuta; Dozens Killed, Military Deployed
analysis.summary: An estimated 60,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta within approximately 24 hours, according to Ceuta's president Juan Jesús Vivas, in one of the largest single-day border crossings in the territory's history. At least 34 people died during the crossings, Spain deployed military forces to reinforce police, and more than 25,000 migrants subsequently returned to Morocco. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez condemned the influx as a violation of Spain's territorial integrity, while Italy announced it was restoring border checks with Spain in response.
